ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended, implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copies of passports of all natural-person shareholders and beneficial owners (UBO KYC pack)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority of the resident jurisdiction, with notarial certification by a notary of that jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / certificate of no bankruptcy (extrait du casier judiciaire or equivalent) of each corporate shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial court, police record authority or company registry of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled power of attorney (procuration) granted by the ultimate shareholders to the incorporating agent or notary representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or consular authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (référence bancaire) confirming source of funds for the share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country credit institution holding the shareholder deposit accounts

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, statutory officers, attorneys-in-fact and any counterparty controlling over EUR 10,000 of annual flows against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) EU consolidated restrictive-measures list; (iii) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists (USD settlement via Stripe/Shopify Payments requires SDN red-flag checks); (iv) the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign Affairs national sanctions and freezing list; and (v) domestic PEP registers under Article 1(24) of the AML Law. Foreign PEPs resident outside the EU/EEA holding more than 10% of shares or management control require enhanced due diligence, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation verified by the notary and bank. The sector is classified bankable AML risk tier Low_Risk_Standard under ISIC 3240 / NAICS 334118, subject to final CDD sign-off; suspicious transactions are reportable to the CRF (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) under Articles 5-6 of the AML Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers portal (lbr.lu), administered by the Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), with pre-clearance also accessible via the eJustice module of guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name may use any language, provided it is written in Latin script; Luxembourg practice requires the legal-form suffix 'S.à r.l.' or the full wording 'société à responsabilité limitée' after the distinctive name. French is the operational filing language of the RCS; any foreign-language name must be accompanied by a French or Luxembourgish transliteration where pronunciation creates a homophone risk. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public policy, or create a likelihood of confusion with a name already registered in the RCS, as set out in Article 2-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915. A trademark pre-clearance across the Benelux Office for Intellectual Property and EUIPO is separately advised for the 'keycap' market brand, although it is not a precondition to RCS registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de commerce / Chambre des métiers
Luxembourg / Lux (when used in a manner implying official or sovereign linkage)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant files the reservation request online via lbr.lu from the start of the pre-incorporation stage. Rejections generally cite: (i) identity or confusing similarity with an existing RCS entry, (ii) use of a protected token without ministerial or professional-body caveat, or (iii) insufficiency of the transliteration. Within 15 days of a rejection notice, the applicant may submit a written rectification or an amended second application through the LBR portal without a new filing fee on the same dossier. If the RCS confirms refusal, the applicant files a reasoned opposition addressed to the RCS registrar (greffier) followed, where necessary, by a commercial chamber appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 40 days of notification, in accordance with the Code of Civil Procedure. A parallel request for ministerial authorization may be required for sensitive tokens listed above; this must be evidenced before the name reservation is granted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this standard-risk e-commerce and manufacturing business, provided the provider is a licensed Luxembourg registered-office company maintaining a physical address in Luxembourg, offering notification and service-of-process capability, and filing the registered-office deregistration notice in the RCS within five business days of any change. A virtual office satisfies the Article 161-1 registered-office requirement of the Law of 10 August 1915; however, VAT, customs (Union Customs Code) and PayPal/Stripe merchant verification may nevertheless require a fuller physical presence record where the entity imports double-shot PBT raw materials. For bank onboarding, the notary and the credit institution will accept a virtual office only with a lease agreement and a registered-office-services undertaking, at a validation cost of approximately EUR 150.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated less than 5% annual probability for a non-regulated, Low_Risk_Standard goods importer/manufacturer). Unannounced inspections at the registered office are not a standard practice of the RCS for non-financial corporate entities; nonetheless, the CRF may issue administrative inspection requests under Article 3-2 of the AML Law, and the RCS may verify existence on complaint or at renewal, so the service provider must operate a physically manned reception point during business hours. Probability rises to moderate (10-20%) if the company triggers enhanced due diligence, e.g., a PEP UBO or sanctioned-jurisdiction payment flows.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, notably Articles 100-1 to 100-183 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR / RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and coordinated articles of association (statuts coordonnés)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 fully subscribed and paid in cash before incorporation; funds must be deposited with a Luxembourg credit institution or held in a notary escrow account with a blocking certificate issued to the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the first meeting of the managers of [●] SARL, the subscribers confirmed that the entire share capital of EUR 12,000.00 has been fully subscribed and paid into a blocked Luxembourg bank account. The managers unanimously resolve: (1) to adopt the deed of incorporation and articles of association as signed before a Luxembourg notary; (2) to adopt the registered office at the address stated in the deed, where the central administration and corporate registers will be kept; (3) to appoint [Name], a Luxembourg resident, as sole manager with day-to-day management authority and sole-signature representation; and (4) to authorise registration with the RCS, publication in the RESA, and all ancillary filing formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS online window (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request through the LBR e-form or attend the RCS counter to verify that the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing company name and does not infringe protected marks. State the intended principal activity as manufacturing of plastic PC keyboard accessories.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of founding subscriber
Name availability application form
Statement of proposed corporate objects and activity codes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected for identity or similarity, file an alternative name application within five working days and revise the constitutional instruments accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarisation of the deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare the deed of incorporation and the statutory articles. Provide the corporate name, registered office address, objects clause covering ISIC 3240 production of plastic keycaps, capital details, subscriber identity, and manager appointment. The notary will verify legal capacity, coordinate the bank certificate and signature meeting.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association approved by subscribers
Identity documents of all subscribers and managers
Lease or domiciliation agreement for the registered office
Bank capital deposit blocking certificate or escrow attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary may request corrected identity or domicile evidence; amend the draft deed and schedule a new signature meeting without need to restart the process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the company account and deposit of registered capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company in formation and deposit not less than EUR 12,000.00. Confirm the source of funds and provide the bank's capital blocking certificate showing the amount, account holder, and blocking instructions until RCS registration of the SARL.
required_dossiers: KYC documents of subscribers and beneficial owners
Proof of source of funds
Draft notarial deed or official request to open a société en formation account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplementary ownership or source-of-funds information, provide an organisational chart and bank statements promptly; use a notary escrow account as an alternative funding route.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation documents with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS registration section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed of incorporation, coordinated articles, bank blocking certificate, registered office declaration, and manager appointment documents to the RCS. The application is made using the official RCS electronic filing procedure; the RCS verifies statutory compliance and assigns the Luxembourg company registration number.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation
Coordinated articles of association
Bank capital blocking certificate
Registered office acceptance or domiciliation declaration
Identity and criminal record certificate of the appointed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: RCS queries are curable within 15 days by delivering the missing certificate or clarifications; the filing is deemed abandoned only if no response is made before the expiry of the procedural deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fiscal, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RCS registration extract and statutes with the ACD to obtain the corporate income tax number and municipal business tax reference. Register with the AEDT for VAT purposes and with the CCSS as a new employer. If the activity requires a commune authorisation, submit the classified establishment application simultaneously.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration (extrait)
Notarial deed and coordinated articles
Identity of managers and directors
Bank account proof
Planned activity description with production capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Each authority acts independently; if one tax registration is delayed, provide the notice to the other administrations and complete the missing declarations under their instruction within 10 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, Direction de l'industrie et de l'innovation, together with the competent commune of the registered office under the law on classed establishments
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Classified Establishment Commune Operating Permit (Autorisation communale d'exploitation d'un établissement classé)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classed establishment, Category 2 – commune authorisation with a simplified environmental impact assessment (évaluation des incidences sur l'environnement) for a small plastic injection unit
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU thresholds applicable to plastic conversion; VOC emissions below the Grand-Ducal Solvent Regulations of 24 November 2003; wastewater discharge in line with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 November 2008 and commune sewerage bylaws; plastic waste transferred only to an authorised waste operator under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by an accredited inspector or the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) verifying fire extinguishers, evacuation routes and alarm systems; structural load inspection certificate confirming floor capacity for injection molding machinery; and occupational health and safety clearance by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM), including workplace ergonomics and accident-prevention measures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration. Main portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) and ACD/AEDT e-Space.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in Luxembourg must file an advance VAT registration application with the AEDT using the official national form, submitted electronically via MyGuichet.lu or by post. If the foreign entity has no fixed establishment, the AEDT may require appointment of a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative. Upon approval, the AEDT assigns a Luxembourg VAT number and a national identification number (matricule). A direct tax registration is additionally required only where a Luxembourg permanent establishment is created; the ACD then registers the entity for corporate income tax and municipal business tax via the matricule system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable as a general pass-through election for a Luxembourg SARL, which is a capital company and tax-opaque. Available statutory elections include: VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 62 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; fiscal unity for corporate income tax purposes under Article 164bis of the Income Tax Law (99% qualifying shareholding and five-year commitment); and specific hybrid mismatch consequential adjustment elections under the 2018 ATAD implementation law. No US-style check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general minimum turnover threshold for established VAT registrants. A small-business exemption applies to undertakings with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT), which may be waived at the taxpayer's option.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based transaction reporting for B2B sales. Electronic invoices are accepted provided authenticity and integrity of origin and content are guaranteed using EDI or advanced electronic signatures. B2G invoicing on public contracts must use the national e-Procurement platform and PEPPOL/EN16931 formats. Luxembourg is monitoring and preparing for the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) reforms, which may introduce digital reporting requirements after 2025.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Luxembourg to destinations outside the European Union are zero-rated under Article 62 of the Luxembourg VAT Law where the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf, evidenced by the customs export declaration and transport documents. Intra-Community supplies to customers holding a valid VAT identification number of another Member State are also zero-rated, provided the goods are dispatched to that Member State and the summary recapitulative statement is filed. Certain offshore services supplied to third-country entrepreneurs fall outside Luxembourg VAT pursuant to place-of-supply rules, thereby being outside the scope rather than expressly zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / Export Accompanying Document EAD)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill or other transport evidence proving dispatch to a third country
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT proof evidencing receipt of export proceeds in Luxembourg)
Packing List and destination customs import evidence where obtainable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The VAT Administration (AEDT) may retrospectively verify export substantiation within the statutory record-keeping and assessment windows. If the taxpayer fails to produce the mandatory export documentation, the zero-rating is reversed and VAT is assessed at 17%, together with late-payment interest and administrative fines under Articles 59 to 64 of the amended VAT Law. Intentional falsification of customs declarations, bills of lading, or remittance evidence constitutes criminal tax fraud under the Luxembourg Criminal Code, punishable by imprisonment and substantial fines. Refund claims based on insufficient export proof are subject to clawback, including interest from the date the refund was paid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting alongside the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and the Ministry of Finance for prudential and anti-money-laundering policy; monetary policy authority is effectively delegated to the European Central Bank within the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains a fully liberalised external financial regime. Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible with no residual exchange controls on the euro or on the repatriation of dividends, profits, or invested capital by non-resident shareholders. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to corporate-law solvency tests (net assets must exceed paid-up capital plus non-distributable reserves) and, where applicable, withholding tax obligations under the law of 4 December 1967 on income tax. No administrative foreign-exchange approval is required for cross-border payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratios apply to export proceeds. Exporters are free to maintain foreign-currency accounts inside or outside Luxembourg. Under European Central Bank balance-of-payments statistical requirements, resident corporates must report individual transactions equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 through their reporting bank; there is no economic obligation to repatriate or convert export receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Corporate Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Corporate Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Corporate Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BCEE – Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Corporate Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) holding a valid Luxembourg or EEA passport may be used for ancillary collections and disbursements, but are not a substitute for a tier-1 credit institution as the primary treasury rail. Non-EEA digital EMIs are generally not viable without authorisation from the CSSF or a recognised passport. In practice, the SARL should rely on a domestic bank for trade finance, liquidity products, and documentary services; fintech EMIs can handle niche flows such as ShopPay or cross-border wallet settlement. Overall viability rating: Medium for ancillary flows, Low as sole treasury clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law and CSSF AML guidance require accurate identification and verification of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners. Most tier-1 banks require at least one physical appearance by the SARL’s manager or a designated signatory, either at the bank branch or with a Luxembourg-based notary / approved financial intermediary. Since the 2022 CSSF digital onboarding guidance, remote video verification is accepted for medium- and low-risk clients under strict conditions, but in practice an in-person interview remains mandatory for corporate clients with non-EEA counterparties. The parent-founder should expect to attend a physical KYC meeting, or appoint a Luxembourg resident professional fiduciary authorised to complete the identification on behalf of the ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction footprint inconsistent with the declared manufacturing activity, e.g., high-frequency prepayments to suppliers in Asia without matching customs or inventory evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide full supply-chain documentation: signed purchase orders, import/export customs declarations, bill-of-lading copies, inventory flow records, Shopify/Stripe sales reconciliations, and manufacturer qualifications of the Chinese or regional resin suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder or beneficial owner is resident in a jurisdiction assessed as high-risk or subject to enhanced due diligence under FATF or EU money-laundering rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a structured ownership chart, passport or residence certificate, source-of-wealth affidavit, bank reference letters from the shareholder’s existing credit institution, and evidence of the originating capital in the form of dividend vouchers or sale-and-purchase agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of evident economic substance, making the SARL appear as an empty conduit rather than a genuine operating manufacturer of custom mechanical keyboard keycaps.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle the operational evidence: lease agreement for the production facility, machinery and double-shot PBT injection moulding equipment purchase or lease documentation, payroll records for technical staff, patent or design registrations for keycap profiles, and tax returns demonstrating ongoing business activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder equity is routed through the notarised subscription phase. The founder or investor transfers the subscribed capital into a blocking account (compte de dépôt de capital) held with a Luxembourg credit institution opened in the name of the SARL in formation. SWIFT transfers must include the exact beneficiary account reference and the notarial deed identification; the purpose code used by the sending bank should identify a direct equity investment (BOP code for inward direct investment) when reporting is required. After incorporation, the released funds are converted into the operational account. No exchange-control approval is required; for non-EEA transfers, the bank will perform standard AML verification of the source of funds and apply the applicable EU sanctions screening. All inbound capital increases are treated similarly, with share premium reported as equity capital.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational payments to foreign suppliers of PBT resin, moulds, keycap stems, and packaging are executed through SWIFT MT103 for transactions below documentary-letter-of-credit thresholds. For high-value mould purchases or recurring procurement from Asia, irrevocable commercial letters of credit (L/C at sight) issued in EUR, USD, or CNY provide settlement security. Intra-EEA suppliers are paid using SEPA Credit Transfer with standard XML payment formats. The SARL’s bank may require underlying invoices and transport evidence for each cross-border disbursement, but does not impose statutory currency conversion restrictions. The bank will screen all beneficiaries against EU, UN, and OFAC sanctions lists; payments to unintended sanctions-affected intermediaries must be restructured through authorised correspondent banks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable over-the-counter currency forwards on leading convertible currencies (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) for firm purchase orders and sales exposure, subject to ordinary credit lines.
Short-dated non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies that are not fully convertible or not deliverable offshore, subject to EMIR margin and central-clearing rules where applicable.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps or plain-vanilla currency swaps under an ISDA/CSA master agreement, used to align future trade receivables and payables with the SARL’s funding currency position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (bilan, compte de profits et pertes, annexes) filed via eCDF in XBRL format
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end; if approval by shareholders occurs later, filing must occur within 1 month of approval. For calendar-year SARL, filing due by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines up to €1,500; persisted failure triggers €7,500 fine per sanction and may lead to court-ordered compliance or administrative strike-off after 1 year of continuous non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (CIT) and municipal business tax (MBT) return – combined form 690
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing for calendar-year SARL due by 31 March of the following year; automatic extension to 30 June for electronically filed returns; further extension to 31 December granted only on documented request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of tax due if underpayment; late tax interest at 0.6% per month; intentional failure assessed at twice the evaded tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual net wealth tax return (form 620) and minimum net wealth tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing for calendar-year SARL due by 31 March; extension aligned with CIT return if jointly filed, but maximum extension to 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default penalty of €500 for non-filing before notice; 10% late reporting penalty; net wealth tax interest accrues at 0.6% per month.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (RBE) – declaration that register of beneficial owners is accurate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – managed by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership; unless no change occurred, the prior declaration remains effective, but a yearly check and confirmation is recommended at year-end. Statutory updating deadline: immediately upon change, not later than 1 month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to €10,000 and imprisonment of 6 months for failure to file or update; publication of non-compliance by RBE.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit required when a SARL exceeds at least two of the three thresholds: balance sheet total €4.4 million, net turnover €8.8 million, average workforce 50 employees. Cash-flow based or single-member SARLs without these thresholds may be exempt and do not appoint an independent auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable général luxembourgeois – PCN) in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002; IFRS optional for consolidated or listed groups and permitted for hotel and commercial companies meeting separate election criteria (SARL after issuance of a ministerial authorization).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: If a controlling shareholder, director, or any beneficial owner changes during the year, the SARL must file a new RBE declaration within 1 month of the change, identifying names, dates of birth, nationality, and particulars of interest (25%+ or control). In the absence of changes, no annual refiling is legally mandated, but a year-end review and internal verification of the registered UBO data must be performed to ensure the RBE record remains accurate; a written confirmation on company letterhead is expected by professional compliance advisors.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (minutes of shareholder and management meetings)
Annual Accounts and Management Reports Archive

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: €1,200–€2,800 per year (approximately $1,300–$3,000) for 24/7 access, mail handling, address use, and physical inspection support in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: €3,500–€7,500 (approximately $3,800–$8,100) for a small SARL undergoing the first full-statutory audit; €1,200–€2,500 for a voluntary auditor opinion or an under-threshold attestation without full audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 80% IP Box exemption on qualified IP income; 95% participation exemption on dividends; 100% capital gains exemption; 8%/2% investment tax credit; 30% digital investment super-deduction; notional interest deduction
